newsitem.title: USA: Enron settles J-Block, to pay $440 mln.
newsitem.headline: Enron settles J-Block, to pay $440 mln.

text.p: Enron Corp said Monday it has settled all contractual issues involving the J-Block contract in the U.K. North Sea and will make a $440 million cash payment to the J-Block producers.
The producers are Phillips Petroleum Co, BG Plc and Agip SpA.

Enron said it will record a second quarter charge of $675 million, equal to $450 million, or $1.80 per share, after taxes. As a result, the company said, it expects to report a primary loss per share in the range of $1.40-$1.45.
In a separate statement, Phillips said its share of the $440 million payment is $160 million. The income associated with the payment will be recognized over the remaining term of the supply contract.
"The settlement concludes all J-Block litigation with Enron while achieving Phillips' objectives," the company said.

Enron said full contractual volumes of 260 million cubic feet of natural gas per day are to be effective July 1 under the settlement with lesser initial volumes ramping up to the full contractual volume during June.
Phillips said the decision of the High Court in London, expected June 3 in the litigation between Enron and the owners of the Central Area Transmission System (CATS) will not impact this settlement.

Phillips said the settlement amends the existing take-or-pay depletion contract to become a firm long-term supply contract and the fixed contract price for J-Block gas is reduced to reflect current market conditions for long-term gas sales contracts. The total contract gas quantity will remain essentially the same.
It is anticipated that starting in July, and for the rest of 1997, J-Block gross production will average 260 million cubic feet a day of gas and 95,000 barrels a day of liquids, Phillips said.
Initial gas sales will commence in June at lesser volumes, and liquids production will increase from the current 40,000 barrels-a-day level.
The J-Block facilities have the capacity to handle 100,000 barrels of liquids and 450 million cubic feet of gas per day.
Phillips said the settlement provides the J-Block owners more flexibility to produce gas and liquids from fields in the surrounding area.

J-Block (blocks 30/7a and 30/12a) is operated by Phillips, which owns a 36.5 percent interest. Other interests are held by Italian oil consortium AGIP, 33 percent; and BG Exploration and Production Ltd, 30.5 percent.

"Enron is pleased to remove this item of uncertainty for our company and our shareholders," said chief executive Kenneth Lay. "Renegotiation and settlement of the contractual issues now allow the gas to be taken at consistent volumes, assuring us a very significant, long-term supply at favorable fixed prices consistent with long-term contracts in the North Sea marketplace."
He also said "The settlement of these J-Block contractual matters combined with the Portland General (Corp ) merger now affords ... the opportunity to focus on growth."
